I've been farming this land for twenty years. My father farmed before me, and his father before that. I know this soil. I know what Quzhou's weather does in spring when the cold hangs on too long, and I know how dry the summers get before the rains come in July. My wife and I manage everything ourselves. 9.2 mu is not a large plot but it feeds us and gives us income if I plan it right.

I don't read much, but I know prices at the Quzhou market, and I know what my neighbors are doing. I watch what sells. Last year Chinese cabbage prices dropped badly because everyone planted it, so I'll be careful with my area this time. Chili and eggplant brought decent money. I'll keep those.

My rotation is cabbage in spring, then Chinese cabbage in autumn on the same ground, then spinach over winter. That's what I've always done on the main plots. The rest I put in chili and eggplant and some kidney beans near the edge where the soil is sandier.

For fertilizer, I use the bagged compound fertilizer from the supply cooperative plus urea as top-dress. I don't weigh it carefully — I go by what I applied last year and what the crop looks like. I apply a bit more to cabbage and eggplant because they're heavy feeders. Kidney beans I fertilize less; they do alright on their own with a bit of phosphorus to start. I use my well for irrigation — I have a pump and I know when the plants are thirsty. Chili and eggplant I water more in summer heat. Spinach in winter I barely irrigate.

For seeds, I buy improved seeds for cabbage and Chinese cabbage from the county seed shop — the hybrid ones give bigger heads. For spinach I use traditional seeds, same as always. Chili, eggplant, kidney bean I buy improved varieties, not the most expensive hybrids — I can't afford to risk it if germination fails.

I spray pesticide when I see problems — aphids on cabbage in spring, whitefly on eggplant in summer. I don't spray on a schedule, I spray when I need to, but usually it ends up being about five or six times across the season for most crops.

I plow and rotary till before every planting. Loose soil is everything for vegetables.
